raw_response:
I've been farming this 9.5 mu for 30 years now. I'm 56, finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says, but at the end of the day I trust what I've seen with my own eyes. My household has seven people — my wife and I, our son and daughter-in-law, and the grandchildren. My son works off-farm at a factory in Handan, so he sends some money home, but we still depend on this land for food and income. That means I can't afford to gamble.

It's almost October now, time to plant wheat. I've got all 9.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's the only system that makes sense here. Last year my wheat did about 460 kg per mu, and the maize hit around 520 kg. Not bad, but fertilizer prices went up again, so I have to watch my spending.

For wheat, I'll plant around October 10th, same as always. I bought improved seed this year — 30 jin per mu, about 15 kg. I usually save my own seed, but last year's looked a bit small, so I spent 45 yuan per mu on fresh seed from the supply shop. The variety is the same one my neighbor Wang uses; he's had good luck with it.

For fertilizer, the extension guy came by and said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough if I apply it right. But three years ago I tried cutting back to 14 kg and my yield dropped to 400 kg. Never again. I'm putting down about 18 kg N per mu total. I'll spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer — the 18-22-5 type — as base before sowing, plus 10 kg of urea mixed in. Then at jointing in March, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I'll topdress another 10 kg of urea. That's two applications. The compound gives me some phosphorus and potassium too, about 11 kg P₂O₅ and 3 kg K₂O per mu. I know the soil is decent here but not rich, so the phosphorus helps with root growth.

Irrigation — I have the well, but pumping costs money. I'll irrigate three times for wheat: once around New Year if the winter is dry, once at jointing in late March, and once at grain filling in early May. Three times at about 15 yuan per mu each time. Four times would be better maybe, but electricity isn't cheap and my son's off-farm money only goes so far.

For pests, I'll spray herbicide once right after planting to control weeds. In spring, if I see aphids, I'll spray insecticide once. I might add fungicide if the weather turns wet and disease shows up — I lost 50 kg per mu to rust five years ago and I'm still angry about it.

Tillage — I'll do rotary tillage before wheat planting. Costs 40 yuan per mu but I don't have my own tractor, so I hire Old Zhang. For maize after harvest, there won't be time to plow. Wheat comes off around June 8th, maize has to go in by June 15th at the latest. I'll chop the stubble and plant direct, no-tillage. Everyone does it that way now.

Labor is mostly family. My wife and I can handle the day-to-day, but for wheat harvest and maize planting in that tight window, I'll hire two or three people for a couple of days. Costs 150 yuan per day now. Total hired labor maybe 6 days across the year. Family puts in about 25 days total — planting, fertilizing by hand, irrigating at night.

For maize, I'll plant hybrid seed — "Nongda 372" or similar, one package per mu, costs about 55 yuan. All the compound fertilizer goes down at planting, about 50 kg per mu of the 28-6-6 blend. That's roughly 14 kg N, 3 kg P₂O₅, and 3 kg K₂O. No topdressing — no time, and honestly the base usually carries it if the summer rains come. I'll irrigate twice: once at seedling stage if June is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage in July. If the rains are good, maybe only once.

Maize pests — corn borer is the main worry. I'll spray insecticide twice, and herbicide once. No-tillage means weeds can be bad if I don't get the herbicide right.

Yield expectation? If the weather is normal, I expect 460 kg per mu for wheat and 530 kg per mu for maize. Not ambitious, just based on what I usually get. I'd rather hit my expectation than dream big and be disappointed.

Total input cost this year will be around 7,200 yuan. That's a lot of money for a family like mine. My son's factory job helps, but if a drought hits or prices crash, we're in trouble. Still, cutting inputs is risky — last year my neighbor Li tried saving 200 yuan on fertilizer and his wheat dropped by 80 kg per mu. Penny wise, pound foolish.
